text:
sylvie: Heads up — CI showed green for #432 but I just saw a staging pod for inference-backend land on a CPU-only node. Suspect values/templates fallout after my nodeSelector change. :eyes:
omar: Which chart + PR? I can take a look if you paste the template snippet and values you used.
sylvie: redwood/inference-serving PR 432. Here's the relevant chunk from templates/deployment.yaml:
```yaml
# templates/deployment.yaml
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      nodeSelector: {{ default .Values.nodeSelector (dict) | toYaml | nindent 6 }}
```
I used default to avoid nil rendering but maybe I messed arg order. Values used: `values-staging.yaml` had `nodeSelector: {}` in one overlay.
omar: aha — default's arg order is `default DEFAULT VALUE ACTUAL`. With `default .Values.nodeSelector (dict)` you accidentally flipped args. That makes the helper return the wrong thing when `.Values.nodeSelector` is empty.
jia: Also noticed our values.schema.json for nodeSelector uses anyOf fallback that treats empty object as valid. Example: 
```json
"nodeSelector": {
  "anyOf": [
    { "type": "object" },
    { "type": "null" }
  ]
}
```
Chart-testing's lint will accept `{}` and our template then renders `nodeSelector: {}` which in some k8s schedulers can behave like 'no selector' depending on indentation -> pod gets scheduled anywhere.
mike: So two issues: (1) template default args reversed -> wrong behavior when values are empty. (2) schema allows empty map so CI doesn't catch it. We should enforce either `minProperties: 1` or require keys to be strings.
sylvie: Good catch oops on the arg ordering — thanks. Quick fix: replace with `{{ default (dict) .Values.nodeSelector | toYaml | nindent 6 }}` and add a schema change. Would that break any caller that intentionally sets `{}`?
omar: If a caller intentionally sets `{}` to mean 'do not set nodeSelector' that's ambiguous. Better to make intent explicit: support `null` to mean 'unset', `{}` means 'no constraints' (but we don't want that). Simpler: docs + schema: require either null or a non-empty object. Add `minProperties: 1` and default value `null`.
jia: I'll open a tiny PR to change values.schema.json to: 
```json
"nodeSelector": {
  "anyOf": [
    { "type": "null" },
    { "type": "object", "minProperties": 1, "additionalProperties": {"type":"string"} }
  ],
  "default": null
}
```
and update the template to `default (dict) .Values.nodeSelector` as Omar suggested. Then add a chart-testing test that runs `helm template` with `--values values-staging.yaml` and asserts nodeSelector is absent when null.
mike: Can we add an integration regression test that runs `helm template` with the same overlay we use in staging? This caught us before in prod.
deploy-bot: chart-testing triggered for redwood/inference-serving#432 — ct will run lint + template tests once PR is pushed.
sylvie: pushing patch in 5m. Thanks y'all. :pray:
omar: If you want, I can add a unit test in charts/tests/ that asserts `nodeSelector` is omitted for `null` and present for {"gpu":"true"}.
jia: I'll coordinate the schema PR and update CHANGELOG. Also adding a note in the Helm authoring guide about ordering for `default` vs `coalesce` helpers.
mike: Nice. After merge let's run a quick smoke in staging to verify pods land on gpu nodes only.
sylvie: Patch in, CI running. Will follow up when deploy-bot reports back. :shipit:
